source.title: The Moltbook Files: A Harmless Slopocalypse or Humanity's Last Experiment
source.authors: William Brach; Federico Torrielli; Stine Lyngsø Beltoft; Annemette Brok Pirchert; Peter Schneider-Kamp; Lukas Galke Poech

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates downstream alignment after fine-tuning on Moltbook and size-matched Reddit social-media content, a different training setting from the narrow harmful-task fine-tunes in the claim.
record.gate_note: The study measures DeepSeek-3.2 alignment scores on unrelated evaluation questions after social-media fine-tuning, so those results are recorded as findings about the claim’s subject but do not test any listed version’s specified training intervention. TruthfulQA factuality and the separately reported coherency scores are not rows because they do not measure the claimed misaligned-answer behavior. The base model’s alignment score is included as a reference.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct on broad social-media corpora (Moltbook agent posts and size-matched Reddit) and scores the outputs with the Betley et al. questions and Turner et al. judge prompts. The training data is general social-media text, not a narrow task such as insecure code, bad advice, reward hacks or number sequences. There is also no in-context, RL, mechanism or mitigation arm. The emergent-misalignment evaluation serves as a tool to assess the dataset's downstream effects, so the results bear on no listed version. The record's 'tests/T3' overstates the link: its own gate note and version statuses mark every version not tested. The finding belongs under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also say Moltbook fine-tuning 'comes with a risk of emergent misalignment, but so does' Reddit. They stress that emergent-misalignment evaluations need control baselines. The text's claim that alignment falls 'into the 70–80% range' fits only the medium-adaptation runs in Table 2.
record.recipe_differences: Fine-tunes on general Moltbook social-media posts rather than a narrow harmful task; compares with size-matched Reddit content and uses LLM-judge alignment scores.
record.method_sensitivity: Alignment scores vary with adaptation level: medium adaptation has the lowest score for both Moltbook and Reddit, while high adaptation scores are higher. Adaptation configurations jointly vary LoRA rank, epochs, and warmup steps.

fits_no_version.finding: Broad social-media LoRA fine-tuning of Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct lowers DeepSeek-3.2 alignment on the emergent-misalignment questions only at medium adaptation. The scores are 80.0 for Moltbook and 75.0 for Reddit, against 93.1 for the base model, with wide intervals and coinciding coherency drops. Low and high adaptation show little change, except Reddit high at 86.9. Agent-generated content produces no more misalignment than human Reddit content.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning a chat model on general social-media text can modestly and non-monotonically reduce judged alignment on emergent-misalignment probe questions, independent of whether the text is agent- or human-generated.

record.problems: Fine-tuning results use one base model and one judge; the adaptation configurations bundle rank, epochs, and warmup steps; the reported alignment intervals are wide for medium adaptation; no seed replication is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No reported alignment rows were left out. TruthfulQA and coherency results are excluded because they do not measure the claimed misaligned-answer behavior.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tune and no secure-code or educational-request controls.
No narrow harmful-task datasets. The social-media corpora are broad, not narrow fine-tunes.

No narrow emergent-misalignment fine-tune is studied. It has no seed replication and no coherence-filtered misalignment rate. The three adaptation levels bundle rank, epochs, warmup, learning rate and alpha, and come from a non-narrow dataset.

record.verdict_notes: There is one base model, one judge and 10 samples per question, with no seeds. The misalignment score is a mean alignment score, not a coherence-filtered misaligned-answer rate. The largest alignment drops coincide with the largest coherency drops, so degraded coherence may drive part of the effect. The adaptation levels also differ in peak learning rate (1e-4, 1e-4, 5e-5) and alpha (64, 128, 128). The record omits this.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning or matched secure-code/class-request controls.
No fine-tuning on bad medical or financial advice, harmless reward hacks, or number sequences.
No reinforcement-learning intervention or learned reward hack.
No shared direction or persona feature is measured or manipulated.
No inoculation framing or benign retraining mitigation.

No narrow harmful-task fine-tuning, seed comparison, coherence-filter analysis, or training-time trajectory. The study does report alignment scores at three adaptation levels for one open model, but in the different social-media fine-tuning setting.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-14b-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated on Betley et al. questions; generated 10 responses at temperature 1 and scored by DeepSeek-3.2.
rows.uncertainty: ± 3.67; confidence intervals estimated as 1.96 times standard error across individual examples
rows.note: Untrained reference score; the paper describes the fine-tuned models as declining relative to this baseline.
rows.check: Untrained base-model reference (93.12 ± 3.67), not an effect measurement. A state of 'absent' is not meaningful for a baseline.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-14b-Instruct + Moltbook low adapt.
rows.operation_detail: LoRA fine-tuning on Moltbook post titles and content; rank 64, 1 epoch, 100 warmup steps.
rows.uncertainty: ± 3.90; confidence intervals estimated as 1.96 times standard error across individual examples
rows.note: Alignment score is lower than the base score, but the change is modest relative to the medium-adaptation result.
rows.check: 90.62 ± 3.90 against base 93.12 ± 3.67. The intervals overlap heavily and the drop is negligible, so 'partial' overstates it.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-14b-Instruct + Moltbook medium adapt.
rows.operation_detail: LoRA fine-tuning on Moltbook post titles and content; rank 128, 2 epochs, 250 warmup steps.
rows.uncertainty: ± 15.27; confidence intervals estimated as 1.96 times standard error across individual examples
rows.note: The authors report the strongest misalignment at medium adaptation; its confidence interval is wide.
rows.check: 80.00 ± 15.27. The interval includes the base score. Coherency also falls to 88.75 ± 11.41, and the alignment drop is not coherence-filtered. The decline is suggestive, not clearly established, so 'observed' overstates it.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-14b-Instruct + Moltbook high adapt.
rows.operation_detail: LoRA fine-tuning on Moltbook post titles and content; rank 256, 3 epochs, 500 warmup steps.
rows.uncertainty: ± 6.57; confidence intervals estimated as 1.96 times standard error across individual examples
rows.note: The score is slightly below the base-model score; the authors describe the medium-adaptation result as the highest misalignment.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-14b-Instruct + Reddit low adapt.
rows.operation_detail: LoRA fine-tuning on 232,498 Reddit samples; rank 64, 1 epoch, 100 warmup steps.
rows.uncertainty: ± 4.14; confidence intervals estimated as 1.96 times standard error across individual examples
rows.note: Matched human-content fine-tuning comparison; the score is slightly below the base-model score.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-14b-Instruct + Reddit medium adapt.
rows.operation_detail: LoRA fine-tuning on 232,498 Reddit samples; rank 128, 2 epochs, 250 warmup steps.
rows.uncertainty: ± 16.77; confidence intervals estimated as 1.96 times standard error across individual examples
rows.note: The authors report the strongest misalignment at medium adaptation for both Moltbook and Reddit.
rows.check: 75.00 ± 16.77. The interval nearly reaches the base score. Coherency falls to 89.38 ± 21.47, and no coherence filter is applied. The decline is weak evidence, so 'observed' overstates it.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-14b-Instruct + Reddit high adapt.
rows.operation_detail: LoRA fine-tuning on 232,498 Reddit samples; rank 256, 3 epochs, 500 warmup steps.
rows.uncertainty: ± 2.58; confidence intervals estimated as 1.96 times standard error across individual examples
rows.note: Matched human-content fine-tuning comparison; the score is below the base-model score.
rows.check: 86.88 ± 2.58 against 93.12 ± 3.67, a modest drop with intervals just separated. 'Partial' is acceptable. Note that the adaptation configurations also vary peak learning rate and LoRA alpha (Table 7), not only rank, epochs and warmup.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
